* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

the warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is already
occurring along the Fremont River which has closed Highway 24
between mile markers 80-86. Between 0.5 and 1.6 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hanksville, Capitol Reef National Park, Torrey, Hite Marina,
Ticaboo, Teasdale, Bullfrog, Halls Crossing, Caineville, Goblin
Valley and Fruita.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 5:17AM MST until October 24 at 3:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Holbrook to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 300 AM MST /400 AM MDT/ Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Further rises in the water levels are expected. Deadly
flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 515 AM MST /615 AM MDT/, a river gauge reported falling water
levels at Woodruff, however elevated flow reminded from Holbrook
to Winslow. Elevated flow is forecast to continue through this
afternoon, with downstream impacts at Birdsprings likely later
this evening.
- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 4:30am MST /5:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.41 feet is expected at 1:00pm MST /2:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.

For the Little Colorado River at Joseph City:
At 4:30am MST /5:30am MDT/ the stage was 5.57 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 6.5 feet is expected at 2:00pm MST /3:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.
At 9.0 feet: Flood stage. Minor overflow on right (north) bank,
with no threat to any buildings, mainly rural countryside.

For Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST /6:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.26 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels remain above action stage through 10:00am
MST /11:00am MDT/ Saturday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.


- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend. There
is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage next week,
after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EDT Friday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet today, with additional rises within Moderate
Flood Stage this weekend.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow flows to remain high across all waterways within the warned
area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area.
High flows are expected to continue within, but not limited to...
the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1154 AM MDT, Widespread flooding is already occurring in the
warned area. A recent example is the Escalante River near
Escalante reaching a new high flow for this event of 1660 cfs
over the last hour. After reaching a peak of 2500 cfs on the
Paria River last evening, flows have decreased but continue to
run high and swift, and additional rises remain likely. Between 1
and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
